source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 45:6 (the Masorah)
claim_en: en charish VE-QATZIR ('no plowing and HARVEST'): the harvest-word stands exactly TWICE in the Torah — the covenant's standing rule 'seed and HARVEST shall not cease' (Gen 8:22) and this decree of five harvestless years — and the Kitzur reconciles the collision on the letter's own terms (named): the covenant promises that what is sown will be reaped; these years none could sow. The corpus's first invariant-versus-narrative collision, resolved without breaking either verse.
middah: E7 (the concordance pair — the same wording at two seats, the Kitzur's reading at narrative strength)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 45:14 (the Ramah; the supercommentaries)
claim_en: TZAVARAV ('his neck'): four tokens in the Torah — the kid-skins on Jacob's DECEIVING neck (27:16), Benjamin's neck at the reunion of the mother's sons (45:14), and the father-reunion pair (46:29, twice in one verse): the neck that deceived a father, the neck of the undeceived brother, the neck of the restored son. Full alef and full yod per the Ramah's rule; the lean form the Mizrachi's text implied exists nowhere (the supercommentaries and MS agree, named).
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 45:16 (the Masorah; the Zohar named)
claim_en: ve-ha-QOL nishma ('and the VOICE was heard' in Pharaoh's house): written LEAN — the Masorah's pair: Ezra's rebuilding-shout 'the voice was heard afar' (Ezra 3:13) FULL: first lean, second full, 'and the secret of the matter is in the Zohar' (MS's own reference, named). The skeleton's other Torah token is Jethro's 'they will LIGHTEN from you' (Exod 18:22) — a homograph collision framed, not claimed.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 45:9 (the Masorah)
claim_en: REDA elai ('come DOWN to me'): ONCE in the Torah; Scripture's pair is the descent-order over Pharaoh's own house — 'go down, and be laid with the uncircumcised' (Ezek 32:19, named): the Kitzur weighs the exile against the pit — the same imperative calls a father down to bread and an empire down to the grave.
middah: E7 (the concordance pair — the same wording at two seats, the Kitzur's reading at narrative strength)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 45:20 (the Masorah's pairs; the Ramah)
claim_en: ve-ENKHEM al tachos ('and let your EYE not spare'): the your-eye word with its second yod LEAN — one of the Masorah's matched one-of-each pairs (the full twin: the garden's 'your eyes will be opened'); this exact form stands ONCE in Scripture. TACHOS lean vav with the precise books against the Torah's otherwise-full spellings (asserted): the unsparing eye, spelled sparingly.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 45:22 (the Hilleli and Yerushalmi copies)
claim_en: CHALIFOT semalot ('changes of garments'): the change-word lives in the Torah ONLY in this verse — twice, with two spellings: the first FULL (chalifot), the second LEAN (chalifot without its vav), each its only token; our books follow the Hilleli's first reading (the Yerushalmi leans both, named): Benjamin's five changes ride the lean word, and the garment-code ends giving.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 45:12 and 45:14 (the printed chilufim rejected)
claim_en: ve-ene achi BINYAMIN ('and the eyes of my brother Benjamin') FULL — the seven-full census's sixth station (G65-02), at the SEEING — while the weeping-necks verse writes the name LEAN twice (45:14, both asserted); and MS REJECTS the printed variance-list's Ben Asher/Ben Naphtali entry at 45:14 by rule: the chilufim do not dispute full-versus-lean spelling (named) — a correction of the books-list itself, carried whole.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 45:25 (the Masorah's five sevirin)
claim_en: va-yavou ERETZ kenaan ('and they came to the LAND of Canaan'): one of the Masorah's FIVE 'presumed' (sevirin) cases — readers presume the directional to-the-land form; the letter writes the bare land and the Masorah locks the resistance: the smoother reading is the marked error.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 45:19 (the Zohar named)
claim_en: ve-ata TZUVETA ('and you are commanded'): written FULL to its final he — 'and it comes for the homily, as it stands in the book of the Zohar' (MS naming his source, named): the king's authorization spelled to its last letter.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai + Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 45:26
claim_en: va-YAGIDU lo ('and they told him') LEAN — the second and last of the Ramah's two lean tellings (the well found, Gen 26:32; the son found, here): the census armed at gen_65 closes at its own station; the Kitzur reads the clipped yod as the clipped telling — they could not tell it whole until the ban of the ten was released (named). VA-YAFAG libo ('and his heart went numb') — the numbing-verb's one Torah token (asserted).
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 45:23 (the Ramah)
claim_en: eser ATONOT noset ('ten she-asses carrying'): the she-ass word lean-of-lean and its carrying-word lean — the Ramah's double-lean rule ('all such she-ass words in this language are lean-of-lean'); the carrying-word's full partner is the Chronicles fleet ('ships carrying', 2 Chr 9:21, named): the lean train carries the full load.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 45:23 (the Masorah)
claim_en: U-MAZON ('and sustenance'): TWICE in Scripture — the father's provision-train (45:23) and Daniel's empire-tree 'and food for all was in it' (Dan 4:9, named): the son feeds the father as the tree feeds all flesh (the Torah-side token checked; the pair named).
middah: E7 (the concordance pair — the same wording at two seats, the Kitzur's reading at narrative strength)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 45:17/21/22/24 (the chapter's file)
claim_en: The chapter's file: TIRGEZU ('quarrel', 45:24) with the gimel DAGESHED (checked); u-LEKHU (45:17) joined by the maqqef against the lengthening-stroke (asserted via the joining); pharaoh's pe soft at the wagons-verse join (45:21), lekhulam (45:22) lamed in qamatz in all books against the patach that Chizkuni's text carried (a books-vs-commentator record, named); the portion's four wagon-tokens counted against the calf-rite's four (the sign between the father and the son, named).
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 93:12
claim_en: A PROPHECY OF TWO SANCTUARIES PRICED AT ONE LETTER, AND THE FORM IS UNIQUE IN THE TORAH. The chain asks why 'he fell on his brother Benjamin's NECK' is written ‹צַוְּארֵי› ('tzavrei,' necks) in the PLURAL - did Benjamin have two necks? - and answers that the two are the two Temples destined for Benjamin's portion and destined to be destroyed, with Benjamin weeping in return over the Tabernacle at Shiloh in Joseph's portion. Machine-checked across the whole Torah: there are NINE neck-tokens, and this construct-plural form stands EXACTLY ONCE, here. Every other seat carries a suffixed form - including the second half of THIS SAME VERSE, where Benjamin weeps on Joseph's neck. The form the reading rests on is a genuine one-off, and the verse itself supplies the control.
middah: ink (necks in the construct plural — the one seat of the form; the two Temples reading beside)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 94:3
claim_en: A FATHER-AND-SON PASSWORD BUILT ON A PUN, AND BOTH ITS ENDS ARE IN THE TORAH. R. Levi reads the wagons ‹עֲגָלוֹת› ('agalot') Joseph sent as a cipher: the last passage father and son studied together was the beheaded heifer ‹עֶגְלָה› ('egla'), so the wagons are the sign that identifies the sender - and the verse names exactly that as what revived the old man's spirit. Machine-checked: the wagon-word stands at SEVEN Torah seats, FOUR of them in this parashah's own units (45:19, 45:21, 45:27, 46:5) and the remaining three in the tribal-prince donation; the heifer-word stands at five, FOUR of them in the beheaded-heifer law of Deuteronomy 21. Both ends of the pun exist in the corpus, in the two places the reading needs them, and the token that carries the recognition is in our ink at the verse the chain cites. Beside it a rule about liars: even when he speaks truth he is not believed - the brothers now paying for the bloodied tunic.
middah: plain (the wagons as the heifer's cipher — a wordplay; both words' seats counted)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 93:10; Bereshit Rabbah 93:11
claim_en: THE SAME ARGUMENT FROM LESSER TO GREATER STATED TWICE BY TWO AUTHORITIES, AND THE UNIT'S OWN VERSE IS ITS MEASURE. Abba Kohen Bardela: if Joseph, youngest of the tribes, rebuked his brothers and they COULD NOT ANSWER HIM (45:3), how much more when the Holy One rebukes each person according to his station. R. Elazar ben Azarya states it independently and sharper: Joseph was flesh and blood and they could not stand; the Holy One is judge, litigant and bench at once. Two sections stating one rule twice, recorded as a standing verdict rather than collapsed as a duplicate - and it argues by the light-and-heavy form ‹קַל וָחֹמֶר› ('kal va-homer,' middah I1) whose own census this corpus seated one block earlier, at 44:8.

check.note: One inference stated independently by two authorities on the same verse, kept as two witnesses rather than reduced to a duplicate.

middah: E5 (if Joseph's rebuke could not be answered, how much more the Holy One's — stated twice)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 93:10
claim_en: THE BODY IS ENTERED AS EVIDENCE, AND THE LANGUAGE IS ENTERED AS CREDENTIAL. 'Come near to me, and they came near' is read as Joseph SHOWING THEM THE CIRCUMCISION - the proof of identity is physical and covenantal at once. In the same passage 'my MOUTH is speaking to you' (45:12) is read as speaking IN THE HOLY TONGUE, the language itself as the credential; Onkelos writes the same reading into the verse, rendering it that I speak to you IN YOUR LANGUAGE. Two independent proofs of identity, one on the body and one in the mouth, and the second is chain-witnessed both ways.

check.note: Identity proven by a bodily sign and by language, the second reading written into the translation as well.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 94:2
claim_en: A RULE FOR INTERPRETING VOWS IS GROUNDED ON THIS VERSE'S INVENTORY. From the three-word provision list at 45:23 - grain, bread and food - R. Yoshiya holds that in vows one follows COLLOQUIAL SPEECH, so each word keeps its plain sense; and Rav Aha bar Eila derives from the word 'food' ‹מָזוֹן› ('mazon') here that ALL foodstuffs fall under the term. Recorded against it is R. Yohanan's own usage, who having eaten boiled grain would say 'I have not eaten food today' - the counter-usage preserved beside the rule it embarrasses. Verified at the ink: the three-word list stands at 45:23 exactly as the argument requires. A vow-interpretation rule for the case-anchored shelf, sourced from a donkey-load of provisions.

check.note: A vow-interpretation rule derived from a three-word provision list, with a contrary usage by a named authority preserved alongside.

middah: plain (in vows follow colloquial speech — the three-word list's plain senses; food covering all foodstuffs)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 94:2
claim_en: THREE TRAVEL RULES READ OUT OF ONE PARTING CLAUSE, AND THE TRANSLATION SUPPLIES THEIR PREMISE. 'Do not be agitated on the way' (45:24) is opened three ways - do not take long strides, do not break off from Torah study, and enter the city while the sun still shines. Onkelos renders the verb as do not be troubled or QUARREL along the way, which is the sense the travel rules assume: a warning about conduct between travellers rather than about fear. Practical law extracted from a farewell.

check.note: Three rules of travel conduct derived from a single parting instruction, with the translation carrying the quarrel sense they presuppose.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

source: Onkelos Genesis 45:27
claim_en: A STATE THIS CORPUS ENTERED FOUR CHAPTERS AGO IS CLOSED BY THE TRANSLATION. Where the verse says 'the SPIRIT of Jacob their father revived,' Onkelos names which spirit: THE SPIRIT OF PROPHECY ‹רוּחַ נְבוּאָה› rested upon him. That closes the claim this project seated at the previous group - that from the day Joseph was taken the Divine Spirit LEFT him, so he would see without seeing and hear without hearing. The departure is read by the midrash at one block and the return is written by the translation at another, the two witnessed by different books, and the machine carries the state across the gap rather than restating it. The only place in the derived corpus where a carried absence is discharged by the buffer rather than by the chain.

check.note: A faculty declared lost at an earlier block and declared returned here by the translation, closing a carried state across four chapters.

middah: ink (the received translation's rendering)

source: Onkelos Genesis 45:28
claim_en: ONE WORD, TWO REFUSALS OF THE PLAIN SENSE. Jacob's ‹רַב› ('rav') at 45:28 could be read 'it is too much.' The chain reads it as GREATNESS - the greatness of my son, who kept his righteousness through more troubles than I bore. Onkelos reads it as JOY - there is great joy for me. The two members of the declared reading disagree with each other and agree in refusing the plain sense, which is the shape this sweep keeps meeting: the dispute is not about the verse's meaning but about which of two better meanings it carries.

check.note: A single ambiguous exclamation read as greatness by the chain and as joy by the translation, both declining the plain sense.

middah: ink (the received translation's rendering)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 94:1
claim_en: A FORWARD SEAT PROMISED FOUR CHAPTERS AGO IS OCCUPIED HERE. It is here, at home, mounted on 'the news was heard in Pharaoh's house' - the household typology in which the tribes are the girls and Joseph the queens. The corpus predicted the seat before deriving the block, and the block arrived carrying it.
